stem.platetectonics.gl_d_accretionary_we: Sediment scraped off a subducting plate onto the overriding plate.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_aftershock: A smaller earthquake that follows a mainshock in the same area.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_anthropocene: Proposed current epoch of human impact.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_asthenosphere: The plastic, partially molten layer of the upper mantle (~100-350 km depth) where plates move.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_atoll: A ring-shaped coral reef around a sunken volcano.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_backarc_basin: An ocean basin formed behind a volcanic arc by extension.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_basalt: Dark volcanic rock. Common in oceanic crust.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_batholith: A very large intrusive igneous body (e.g., Sierra Nevada batholith).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_blueschist: A low-temperature high-pressure metamorphic rock; subduction zone marker.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_caldera: A large, basin-shaped depression formed when a volcano collapses after a major eruption (e.g., Yellowstone, Crater Lake).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_cinder_cone: A small, steep volcano built from ejected ash and cinders (e.g., Paricutin, Sunset Crater).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_cleavage: Pattern of breaking in mineral or rock.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_continental_cru: The lower-density, thicker crust beneath continents; ~30-70 km thick.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_continental_dri: Theory that continents move over geological time. Proposed by Wegener.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_continental_ris: Gentler slope at base of continent.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_continental_she: Submerged extension of a continent; gently sloping.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_continental_slo: Steeper edge of a continent leading from shelf to deep ocean.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_convection: The transfer of heat by movement of fluid; drives plate motion in the mantle.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_convection_curr: Heat-driven flow in mantle. Drives plate motion.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_convergent_boun: Where two plates push together; produces mountains, trenches, and volcanic arcs.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_core: Innermost layer. Outer core liquid, inner core solid.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_craton: An ancient and stable interior of a continent (e.g., Canadian Shield, Baltic Shield).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_crust: Outer rocky layer. Continental (lighter, thicker) or oceanic (denser, thinner).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_crustal_recycli: The process by which crustal material returns to the mantle at subduction zones.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_crystal_system: Geometry class. Cubic, tetragonal, hexagonal, etc.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_decollement: A near-horizontal fault surface separating deformed rocks above from undeformed below.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_density: Mass per unit volume. Differentiates rock types.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_diffuse_plate_b: A wide zone where deformation is distributed rather than localized.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_dike: A vertical or steeply-dipping intrusion of magma cutting across rock layers.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_divergent_bound: Where two plates move apart; produces mid-ocean ridges and continental rifts.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_earthquake: Sudden release of energy along a fault.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_eclogite: A high-pressure metamorphic rock formed from subducted oceanic crust.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_epicenter: The point on Earth surface directly above an earthquake focus.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_euler_pole: The point about which a tectonic plate rotates relative to another.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_exotic_terrane: A terrane that originated far from its current location.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_fault: A fracture in Earth crust along which rocks have moved.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_focus_hypocente: Point below ground where earthquake originates.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_fore_arc_basin: A sedimentary basin between a trench and volcanic arc.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_foreland_basin: A depression formed in front of an advancing mountain range.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_foreshock: A smaller earthquake that precedes a mainshock in the same area.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_fracture: Pattern of breaking without preferred direction.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_fumarole: A vent emitting steam and volcanic gases.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_geothermal_grad: Rate of temperature increase with depth in Earth (~25 C/km in crust).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_geyser: A hot spring that periodically erupts steam and hot water.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_glacial_isostat: Land slowly rising after melting of glacial ice loaded it down.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_gondwana: Southern supercontinent: Africa, South America, Antarctica, Australia, India.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_granite: Light intrusive rock. Common in continental crust.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_guyot: A flat-topped seamount; eroded former island, then subsided.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_hotspot: A localized region of upwelling mantle that produces volcanism (e.g., Hawaii, Yellowstone).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_hotspot_track: A chain of progressively older volcanoes formed as a plate moves over a hotspot.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_hydrothermal_ve: Underwater hot spring at mid-ocean ridges; supports chemosynthetic life.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_hypocenter_focu: The actual underground location where an earthquake originates.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_intensity: A measure of earthquake shaking effects at a location (Mercalli scale); varies by site.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_iridium_anomaly: High Ir layer at K-T boundary. Asteroid evidence.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_island_arc: A volcanic arc formed where two oceanic plates converge (e.g., Mariana, Tonga).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_isostasy: The balance between Earth crust and mantle; like icebergs floating in water.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_k_t_boundary: Cretaceous-Tertiary mass extinction 65 Ma. Asteroid + volcanism.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_lahars: Volcanic mudflows; can travel far and fast, very destructive.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_laurasia: Northern supercontinent: North America and Eurasia (minus India).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_lava: Molten rock that has reached Earth surface.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_liquefaction: Solid ground behaves like liquid during earthquake.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_lithosphere: The rigid outer shell of Earth, including crust and uppermost mantle (~0-100 km).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_luster: How light reflects from mineral surface.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_magnetic_revers: A complete flip of Earth magnetic field (averages ~250,000 years between reversals).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_magnitude: A measure of earthquake size based on the seismic waves it generates. Logarithmic scale.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mantle: Layer between crust + core. Mostly solid but flows over time.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mantle_plume: A column of hot mantle rising from deep within Earth that creates hotspots.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mantle_viscosit: Resistance to flow in the mantle; varies with depth and temperature.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mantle_wedge: The wedge-shaped piece of mantle between a subducting slab and overriding plate.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mass_extinction: Catastrophic loss of biodiversity. 5 major events.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mercalli_intens: Scale of earthquake damage at specific location.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_microplate: A small tectonic plate (e.g., Juan de Fuca, Caribbean).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mid_ocean_ridge: Underwater mountain range where new ocean crust forms at divergent boundaries.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mineral: Naturally occurring inorganic solid with specific composition.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_moho: The Mohorovicic discontinuity; boundary between crust and mantle.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_mohs_hardness_s: Scale 1-10 of mineral hardness. Talc to diamond.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_moment_magnitud: Modern scale used for all earthquake sizes; supplants Richter for large events.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_normal_fault: A fault where the hanging wall drops down relative to the footwall; tensional.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_oblique_slip_fa: A fault with both horizontal and vertical motion.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_oceanic_crust: The denser, thinner crust beneath oceans; ~5-10 km thick.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_ophiolite: A section of oceanic crust and upper mantle thrust onto a continent during collision.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_outer_core: Liquid iron-nickel layer (~2900-5100 km depth); source of magnetic field.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_p_wave: Primary wave; compressional; fastest seismic wave; travels through solids and liquids.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_paleomagnetism: The study of ancient magnetic field directions preserved in rocks.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_pangaea: Supercontinent assembled by ~300 million years ago; broke apart starting ~200 Ma.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_permian_triassi: Largest ever extinction 252 Ma. ~96% marine species lost.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_pillow_lava: Bulbous lava formed when basalt erupts underwater.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_plate_boundary: The edge of a tectonic plate where it meets another plate; can be divergent, convergent, or transform.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_plate_reconstru: Models of past plate positions based on geological and paleomagnetic data.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_plate_tectonics: Theory that lithosphere is broken into plates that move.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_plate_velocity: Speed of plate motion in cm per year; fastest ~24 cm/yr (Pacific-Tonga); slowest ~1 cm/yr.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_pluton: A smaller igneous intrusion than a batholith.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_pumice: Light rock with many gas bubbles.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_pyroclastic_flo: A fast-moving cloud of hot gas and volcanic debris; one of the deadliest volcanic hazards.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_reverse_thrust_: A fault where the hanging wall moves up relative to the footwall; compressional.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_richter_magnitu: The original 1935 logarithmic scale of earthquake size; each unit = 10x amplitude. It saturates above about M7, so moment magnitude is used for large quakes.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_richter_scale: Original 1935 magnitude scale; works well for small or local quakes; saturates above M7.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_ridge_push: A force from elevated mid-ocean ridges sliding plates away.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_rift: A continental zone where the crust is being pulled apart (e.g., East African Rift).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_ring_of_fire: Pacific volcanic + seismic zone. 75% of world's volcanoes.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_s_wave: Secondary wave; shear; slower than P; travels only through solids.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_seafloor_spread: New ocean crust forms at ridges. Plates push apart.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_seamount: An underwater mountain rising from the seafloor; usually volcanic.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_seismic_moment: A measure of earthquake size based on fault area times slip times rigidity.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_seismic_wave: Energy wave from earthquake. P + S + surface waves.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_seismograph: Instrument that records ground motion during an earthquake.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_shield_volcano: A broad, gently sloping volcano built from low-viscosity basaltic lava (e.g., Mauna Loa).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_sill: A horizontal intrusion of magma between rock layers.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_slab_pull: A force from a dense subducting slab pulling the rest of the plate behind it.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_slab_rollback: Backward motion of a subducting slab; causes overriding plate extension.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_solfatara: A volcanic vent emitting sulfurous gases.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_stratovolcano: A steep-sided, conical volcano built from alternating layers of lava and ash (e.g., Fuji, Mt St Helens).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_stratovolcano_c: The classic volcanic mountain shape: tall, steep, alternating ash and lava.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_strike_slip_fau: A fault where blocks slide horizontally past each other (e.g., San Andreas).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_subduction: One plate slides under another. Forms trenches + volcanoes.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_subduction_zone: A convergent boundary where one plate dives beneath another, recycling crust into the mantle.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_supercontinent: Single landmass containing most continental crust.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_supervolcano: Volcano capable of producing >1000 km³ of erupted material.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_surface_wave: Seismic wave traveling along Earth surface; causes most damage (Love, Rayleigh).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_suture_zone: A zone where two continents collided and joined (e.g., Indus-Tsangpo, Urals).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_tectonic_plate: Rigid lithospheric segment that moves over asthenosphere.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_tephra: Fragmental material ejected by a volcano; ash, lapilli, blocks.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_terrane: A fragment of crust with a distinct geological history accreted to a larger landmass.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_transform_bound: Where two plates slide past each other (e.g., San Andreas Fault).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_trench: A deep, narrow depression in the ocean floor at a subduction zone.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_triple_junction: Where three plate boundaries meet (e.g., Afar Triangle).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_tsunami: A series of ocean waves caused by underwater displacement (quake, landslide, eruption, impact).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_underplating: Addition of magma or sediment to the base of crust.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_volcanic_arc: A chain of volcanoes formed parallel to a subduction zone (e.g., Cascades, Aleutians).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_volcanic_bomb: A blob of molten rock ejected during an eruption.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_volcanic_gas: Gases released during volcanic eruptions; mainly H2O, CO2, SO2.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_volcanic_neck: Solidified magma in a volcano throat, exposed by erosion (e.g., Devils Tower).
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_welded_tuff: Pyroclastic rock formed when hot ash particles fuse on landing.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_wilson_cycle: Repeated opening + closing of ocean basins, in cycles of roughly 500 million years. Coined by J.T. Wilson.
stem.platetectonics.gl_d_xenolith: A foreign rock fragment incorporated into magma; samples the deep crust or mantle.
